text:
Anya (PM): quick heads-up — FinCo asked for per-tenant burst safeguards + clearer autoscale hysteresis before they sign Dedicated contract. can we scope a small, shipable thing?
Michael (Eng): can you list must-haves vs nice-to-haves? helps estimate.
Anya (PM): must-have: enforceable burst cap per tenant (hard cap) + telemetry/export; must-have: autoscale cooldown tunables per pool. nice: predictive prewarm, UI for burst history, billing export.
Raj (SRE): ops constraints: we need per-tenant token counters live in the routing layer, and a fast path to reject over-cap requests to avoid head-of-line impacts. also alerts for spillover.
Michael (Eng): implementation idea: add token_bucket per-tenant keyed in request router + shared fallback routing to preemptible pool. cheap runtime check.
Sophia (ProdOps): FinCo also wants SLA language: 95th latency target on committed pool when under cap, and explicit statement fallback behavior (soft-spill -> rate limit -> reject).
Anya (PM): acceptance criteria proposal:
- config: per-tenant burst_cap_tokens (integer) settable via console/api
- enforcement: requests that exceed burst cap return 429 with `x-redwood-reason: burst_cap`
- telemetry: per-tenant metrics (tokens_used, cap_hits, average_latency) plus an export for billing daily
- autoscale: separate `cooldown_seconds` and `min_nodes` per pool
- docs: runbook for oncall + customer-facing FAQ
Michael (Eng): rough tasks: router token-bucket + metrics (2 wks), 429 path + error codes (1 wk), console CRUD (1 wk), autoscale knobs plumbing (1 wk). total ~5w sprints but can parallelize.
Raj (SRE): oncall: add alert if `cap_hits_rate` > 5% sustained for 5m and fallback traffic > 10rps. also need a dry-run mode to roll out enforcement safely.
Anya (PM): agree dry-run needed. propose rollout plan:
- alpha: internal and FinCo opt-in, enforcement off, telemetry-only (2w)
- beta: dry-run enforcement (logs + 429 simulation) (1w)
- GA: hard enforcement + billing export (1w)
Sophia (ProdOps): commercial: FinCo will pay for prewarm add-on if we ship predictive prewarm later. recommend selling Phase 1 as governance + Phase 2 as performance add-on.
Michael (Eng): question on predictive prewarm: do we need ML infra first or can we use simple heuristics (rate window + spike detector) to start? heuristics quicker.
Anya (PM): start with heuristics under Phase 2, mark ML predictor as next-6mo.
Raj (SRE): checklist for GA ops readiness:
```
- dry-run observed for 72h with <1% false positive rejections
- oncall playbook tested in chaos window
- dashboards for cap usage and latencies in last 7d
- alert runbook: escalation path + customer comms template
```
Sophia (ProdOps): launch docs: include example customer contract language and prewarm pricing tiers.
Anya (PM): decision needed: do we include per-tenant `soft_spill` flag (allow queued prewarm attempts) in Phase 1 or cut to Phase 2? opinions?
Michael (Eng): lean cut to Phase 2 — adds complexity in router state and queuing. Phase 1 simpler and faster.
Raj (SRE): +1 cut to Phase 2. want the enforcement semantics nailed before adding queueing.
Sophia (ProdOps): FinCo pushes for soft_spill but will accept roadmap timeline if we give clear dates. set Phase 2 target in 6w after GA.
Anya (PM): ok consensus: Phase 1 = cap + telemetry + autoscale knobs + dry-run + ops runbook. Phase 2 = soft_spill + predictive prewarm + UI + billing export improvements. I'll draft PRD and run it by legal/commercial for SLA wording.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: staging -> canary next Tuesday 03:00 UTC (reminder) :calendar: 
Michael (Eng): allocating eng lead (me) and one backend IC. will spin up RFC with config schema.
Anya (PM): thanks — I'll add FinCo contacts and put timeline in the PRD. leaving this thread open until PRD review done. :thumbsup:
